info.title: Maven Java project with logging facade

diffs.patch:
Index: pom.xml
===================================================================
--- pom.xml	
+++ pom.xml	
@@ -0,0 +1,75 @@
+<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
+<project xmlns="http://maven.apache.org/POM/4.0.0"
+         xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance"
+         xsi:schemaLocation="http://maven.apache.org/POM/4.0.0 http://maven.apache.org/xsd/maven-4.0.0.xsd">
+    <modelVersion>4.0.0</modelVersion>
+
+    <groupId>com.example</groupId>
+    <artifactId>demo-app</artifactId>
+    <version>1.0.0-SNAPSHOT</version>
+    <packaging>jar</packaging>
+
+    <name>demo-app</name>
+    <description>Maven Java application using SLF4J as its logging facade.</description>
+
+    <properties>
+        <maven.compiler.release>21</maven.compiler.release>
+        <project.build.sourceEncoding>UTF-8</project.build.sourceEncoding>
+
+        <slf4j.version>2.0.16</slf4j.version>
+        <logback.version>1.5.16</logback.version>
+        <junit.version>5.11.4</junit.version>
+    </properties>
+
+    <dependencies>
+        <!-- Logging facade: application code compiles against this only. -->
+        <dependency>
+            <groupId>org.slf4j</groupId>
+            <artifactId>slf4j-api</artifactId>
+            <version>${slf4j.version}</version>
+        </dependency>
+
+        <!--
+            Runtime binding. Swap this single dependency to change the logging
+            implementation (e.g. log4j-slf4j2-impl) without touching app code.
+        -->
+        <dependency>
+            <groupId>ch.qos.logback</groupId>
+            <artifactId>logback-classic</artifactId>
+            <version>${logback.version}</version>
+            <scope>runtime</scope>
+        </dependency>
+
+        <dependency>
+            <groupId>org.junit.jupiter</groupId>
+            <artifactId>junit-jupiter</artifactId>
+            <version>${junit.version}</version>
+            <scope>test</scope>
+        </dependency>
+    </dependencies>
+
+    <build>
+        <plugins>
+            <plugin>
+                <groupId>org.apache.maven.plugins</groupId>
+                <artifactId>maven-compiler-plugin</artifactId>
+                <version>3.13.0</version>
+            </plugin>
+
+            <plugin>
+                <groupId>org.apache.maven.plugins</groupId>
+                <artifactId>maven-surefire-plugin</artifactId>
+                <version>3.5.2</version>
+            </plugin>
+
+            <plugin>
+                <groupId>org.codehaus.mojo</groupId>
+                <artifactId>exec-maven-plugin</artifactId>
+                <version>3.5.0</version>
+                <configuration>
+                    <mainClass>com.example.app.App</mainClass>
+                </configuration>
+            </plugin>
+        </plugins>
+    </build>
+</project>

Index: src/main/resources/logback.xml
===================================================================
--- src/main/resources/logback.xml	
+++ src/main/resources/logback.xml	
@@ -0,0 +1,12 @@
+<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
+<configuration>
+    <appender name="CONSOLE" class="ch.qos.logback.core.ConsoleAppender">
+        <encoder>
+            <pattern>%d{yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm:ss.SSS} [%thread] %-5level %logger{36} - %msg%n</pattern>
+        </encoder>
+    </appender>
+
+    <root level="INFO">
+        <appender-ref ref="CONSOLE"/>
+    </root>
+</configuration>

parts.text:
Empty project. Let me create a standard Maven Java project with SLF4J API as the facade, plus a runtime implementation. Since the user wants the application code not tied to one implementation, the key is using SLF4J API. For a runnable app we need a backend binding. The standard modern choice is Logback or Log4j2. I'll include SLF4J API as compile dependency and Logback classic as runtime dependency.

Let me pick Java 17 for broad compatibility (though Java 26 available). Actually let's use Java 17 as a safe LTS. Or 21 LTS. I'll use 21.

Let me create:
- pom.xml
- src/main/java/com/example/app/App.java
- src/main/resources/logback.xml
- src/test/java/com/example/app/AppTest.java
- .gitignore

Let me create a proper package. Group id com.example, artifact demo-app.

Let me write files. I should use the latest stable SLF4J (2.0.x) and Logback 1.5.x. Latest known: slf4j 2.0.16, logback 1.5.16. Let me use those. Also JUnit 5.

Let me create the todo list since it's multi-step. Actually it's moderately multi-step. Let me just do it.

Let me verify build after.
Empty project with Java 26 and Maven available. I'll create a Maven project using **SLF4J** as the logging facade and **Logback** as the runtime binding (swappable without touching app code).

input.content:
<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
<project xmlns="http://maven.apache.org/POM/4.0.0"
         xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance"
         xsi:schemaLocation="http://maven.apache.org/POM/4.0.0 http://maven.apache.org/xsd/maven-4.0.0.xsd">
    <modelVersion>4.0.0</modelVersion>

    <groupId>com.example</groupId>
    <artifactId>demo-app</artifactId>
    <version>1.0.0-SNAPSHOT</version>
    <packaging>jar</packaging>

    <name>demo-app</name>
    <description>Maven Java application using SLF4J as its logging facade.</description>

    <properties>
        <maven.compiler.release>21</maven.compiler.release>
        <project.build.sourceEncoding>UTF-8</project.build.sourceEncoding>

        <slf4j.version>2.0.16</slf4j.version>
        <logback.version>1.5.16</logback.version>
        <junit.version>5.11.4</junit.version>
    </properties>

    <dependencies>
        <!-- Logging facade: application code compiles against this only. -->
        <dependency>
            <groupId>org.slf4j</groupId>
            <artifactId>slf4j-api</artifactId>
            <version>${slf4j.version}</version>
        </dependency>

        <!--
            Runtime binding. Swap this single dependency to change the logging
            implementation (e.g. log4j-slf4j2-impl) without touching app code.
        -->
        <dependency>
            <groupId>ch.qos.logback</groupId>
            <artifactId>logback-classic</artifactId>
            <version>${logback.version}</version>
            <scope>runtime</scope>
        </dependency>

        <dependency>
            <groupId>org.junit.jupiter</groupId>
            <artifactId>junit-jupiter</artifactId>
            <version>${junit.version}</version>
            <scope>test</scope>
        </dependency>
    </dependencies>

    <build>
        <plugins>
            <plugin>
                <groupId>org.apache.maven.plugins</groupId>
                <artifactId>maven-compiler-plugin</artifactId>
                <version>3.13.0</version>
            </plugin>

            <plugin>
                <groupId>org.apache.maven.plugins</groupId>
                <artifactId>maven-surefire-plugin</artifactId>
                <version>3.5.2</version>
            </plugin>

            <plugin>
                <groupId>org.codehaus.mojo</groupId>
                <artifactId>exec-maven-plugin</artifactId>
                <version>3.5.0</version>
                <configuration>
                    <mainClass>com.example.app.App</mainClass>
                </configuration>
            </plugin>
        </plugins>
    </build>
</project>

<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
<configuration>
    <appender name="CONSOLE" class="ch.qos.logback.core.ConsoleAppender">
        <encoder>
            <pattern>%d{yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm:ss.SSS} [%thread] %-5level %logger{36} - %msg%n</pattern>
        </encoder>
    </appender>

    <root level="INFO">
        <appender-ref ref="CONSOLE"/>
    </root>
</configuration>

parts.text:
Done. The build, tests, and app all run.

```
pom.xml
src/main/java/com/example/app/App.java
src/main/resources/logback.xml
src/test/java/com/example/app/AppTest.java
.gitignore
```

Key point for the facade requirement: `App.java` imports only `org.slf4j.*`. The backing implementation (`logback-classic`) is a `runtime` dependency, so swapping in Log4j2 means changing one dependency block — no application code changes.

Commands: `mvn verify` (build+test), `mvn exec:java` (run).
